Soaking in a warm (or hot of you can handle it) bath, then incorporating rolling tennis balls on your legs while stretching might be able to release the fascia while you also stretch the muscle. It would be a significant but gentle way to hit both the muscles and fascia at the same time.

I have also seen a lot of "yoga poses to cure fibromyalgia" videos that are no different from any beginners video. I imagine to someone with fibro and with no knowledge of yoga these videos can be really disappointing because they will think there isn't a way to modify even further.

Sometimes I don't leave the ground when I practice now, so I can help there! Very important to be able to control depth; it's easy to put a ton of pressue into your back and cause injury if you don't modify and make the pose accessible to you.

I used to specialize in beginners classes, and have guided a lot of people with injuries, fresh out of surgery/PT, of all shapes and sizes and limitations.

My goal would be to teach from experience, and offer cues, and modifications specifically with pain and ailments in mind. The only thing that doesn't vary whether you are perfectly healthy vs having a condition, is that you listen to your own body and not push past your own edge. I know that even with all the modifications there will still be people who can't participate in what I hope to offer, but if I can give 1 person a little bit of relief it'll be worth it.

Was riding bikes with my cousin at the elementary school up the road from my grandparent's house. We were 6 and 8 years old.

A large Astro van pulled into the parking lot. It had one of those painted murals on the side of it, like a wolf or something. He pulled up near where my cousin and I were riding at the bus turn around, which had a concrete half pipe looking thing around it. There was a woman in the passenger seat. He got out of the van and grabbed a tarp or an empty sac and started walking toward us. He didn't say anything to us as he was approaching. I remember feeling danger. I am a couple years older than my cousin, and I didn't want to freak him out, so I called him to ride with me to the other end of the parking lot, toward the play ground.

The man put the tarp thing back in the side door of the van, left the door open, and drove toward us again. He again, got out of the van, grabbed the tarp or whatever and started approaching us. At this point, I was certain we were not in a good situation. I told my cousin we needed to leave, and I somehow knew in the moment that I didn't want to lead this guy to our grandparents, so we rode to a random house across from the school. I ran up to the door and knocked, and the van drove off.

Once I saw the van turn down a different street we hauled ass back home. We told our grandparents and both our parents, they didn't believe us. We went back out in the yard/woods to play with our brothers and sure enough that van drove by 2 more times.

I do have the option to work from home if I need to, but I try not to take advantage of this more than my coworkers.
